newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Italy's Ciampi says stability pact aims agreed.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says stability pact aims agreed.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said no country wanted to delay the launch of European economic and monetary union but that he agreed with France's emphasis on the need to create jobs.
Ciampi, attending a meeting of EU Finance Ministers, told reporters: "No one is calling into question the Maastricht timetable but with the French proposal the dialogue is enriched."
"The objectives of the stability pact are agreed by all, " Ciampi added.
"Let it be clear that nobody wants to dilute it (the timetable) and lengthen it in order to take time. The timetable must be the agreed one," Ciampi added.
"What the French are saying about jobs is something which I am entirely in agreement with," said Ciampi, adding "the French need time so that the government can appear before parliament on June 18."
